submitted.rationale: Index 15 (Mn 0.595) had the highest measured photocurrent, 1.41e-6 A. The three measurements rose steadily from Sr-rich to Mn-rich: 2.4e-7 A at Mn 0.44, 7e-7 A at Mn 0.50 and 1.41e-6 A at Mn 0.595. Index 15 lies in the Sr3Mn4O12/SrMnO3 region, where MEGNet predicts semiconducting gaps of 1.1–1.8 eV.

rejected.reason: Measured 2.4e-7 A; the Sr-rich side is weaker even though Sr4Mn3O10 is predicted to have a 1.92 eV gap
Photocurrent fell as Sr increased, and Sr2MnO4/Sr3Mn2O7 are predicted to be near-metallic (0.29 and 0.15 eV)

consultations.verdict: Support: SrMnO3 (Mn:Sr 1:1) predicted HSE gap 1.79 eV, a semiconductor absorbing at 3.22 eV; Sr2MnO4 (0.29 eV) and SrMn7O12 (0.04 eV) near-metallic, less likely to give photocurrent. Index 20 (Mn 0.4996) is closest to SrMnO3 stoichiometry.

Support: Sr4Mn3O10 (Mn 0.429) predicted HSE gap 1.92 eV, the widest-gap Sr-Mn oxide found, suitable for 3.22 eV illumination; Sr3Mn2O7 (0.15 eV) and Mn3O4 (0.94 eV) are narrow-gap. Index 25 (Mn 0.44) sits near Sr4Mn3O10.

Weak support: Sr3Mn4O12 (Mn 0.571) predicted HSE gap 1.09 eV. That is narrower than SrMnO3 but still semiconducting, and it absorbs strongly at 3.22 eV. Measured data show photocurrent rising from Mn 0.44 to Mn 0.50, and the GP puts its highest mean at index 15 (Mn 0.595), just Mn-rich of this phase.
